subject: Dedicated vs Private capacity — sizing & procurement next steps for Orion Health
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@orionhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing note — initial capacity targets

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from our procurement side: we need a clearer comparison between Dedicated (reserved Redwood capacity) and Private (VPC/on‑prem) options for our regulated workloads.

Key constraints that will drive the decision:
- All PHI processing must be isolated from multi-tenant environments.
- Audit logs retained for 7 years; links to KMS/HSM mandatory.
- Target latency for inference: p95 < 180ms for 256-token prompts.
- Monthly peak concurrency expected: 120 simultaneous sessions during batch windows.

Can you share a short sizing and cost tradeoff we can attach to the procurement packet? Also want to confirm lead time for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) vs a Private deployment.

Appreciate it,
Samantha
Procurement Lead — Orion Health

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing note — initial capacity targets

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the clear constraints. I've looped in Karthik (solutions) and Rishi (sales lead). We put together a concise comparison and an initial sizing workbook; attaching now. High-level answer up front:

- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): faster time-to-provision (typically 2–4 weeks for standard pools in public regions), predictable per-token economics, full Redwood-managed runtime. Viable if you want minimal ops overhead and strong SLA. Offers tenant isolation via dedicated GPU pools and data isolation controls.

- Private (VPC / On‑prem): better for customers requiring full control of network, KMS/HSM in their VPC, and air-gapped compliance. Longer lead time (4–10+ weeks depending on on‑prem hardware procurement), higher up-front engineering and onboarding effort, but lowest residual compliance risk.

Karthik will follow with sizing estimates (GPU types & counts) mapping to your concurrency and latency targets. If you prefer, we can produce two purchase options in the quote: a 12‑month Dedicated commit and a Private onboarding + support package.

Next steps: Karthik — please add the technical sizing and an ops checklist (NTP, KMS endpoints, audit log feed). Rishi — can you confirm pricing cadence and whether we can include a short-term ramp credit to bridge onboarding?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-sizing.xlsx (see Karthik's worksheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing note — initial capacity targets

Samantha — quick technical addendum and assumptions (see attached workbook for calculations).

Assumptions:
- Typical prompt length: 256 tokens. Completion average: 128 tokens.
- p95 latency target: <180ms at 256 tokens.
- Peak concurrency: 120 simultaneous interactive sessions; sustained background batch of 400 qps for nightly processing (non-real-time).
- Model: MPT-7B-quant (baseline) and a fall-back to MPT-13B for high-quality responses.

Sizing recommendation (high-level):
- Dedicated configuration (cost-optimized):
  - 8x A10G-class GPUs in a single dedicated pool for interactive load (continuous batching + KV cache). Expected p95 ~140–170ms for 256 tokens on MPT-7B-quant with our runtime.
  - 2x A100s for peak burst / heavy rerank jobs (nightly batches).
  - Autoscale policy: maintain 6 GPUs, burst to 10 during peak windows.
  - Estimated sustained throughput: ~480 concurrent gen QPS (smallest batch size optimization applied).

- Private configuration (compliance-first):
  - On‑prem specification: 6x A100 40GB (mixed-use) with local NFS for checkpointing; Redwood private runtime deployed inside customer VPC. Latency target achievable; slightly better tail behavior due to local network.
  - Requires customer procurement of GPUs (order lead ~6–10 weeks) or we can recommend partner hardware with financing.

Tradeoffs summary:
- Time to value: Dedicated wins (2–4 weeks) vs Private (6–10+ weeks).
- Operational lift: Redwood manages Dedicated; Private requires initial infra & networking work (NAT, KMS integration, logging pipelines).
- Unit cost: Dedicated lower OPEX if commit is sizable; Private has higher initial CAPEX but gives stronger isolation guarantees.
- Compliance surface: Private reduces compliance risk for air-gapped requirements and satisfies stricter KMS/HSM placements.

Ops checklist (short):
- KMS/HSM endpoints and signing certs
- SSH bastion strategy for access windows
- Log forwarding endpoint (S3/ELK) + retention policy
- Network ACLs and peering configuration

I attached a spreadsheet with three sizing scenarios: conservative (50% buffer), expected, and aggressive (2x concurrency). Please review and tell us which scenario matches procurement's risk appetite.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-sizing.xlsx

Team —

Thanks for the quick sizing. A couple of follow-ups from security/compliance before procurement proceeds:

1) For the Dedicated option, can you confirm where KMS keys are stored and whether we can bring our own key (BYOK) for tokenization/encryption? We need explicit support for HSM-backed keys and single-tenant key boundaries.

2) Audit logs: you mentioned we could integrate a log-forwarder — can you provide sample retention policies and raw log formats? We will need immutable logs for 7 years.

3) Private deployment questions: who owns patching for the runtime and how are security bulletins communicated? Also require an escalation path for an incident response (contact + SLO).

Please mark answers inline and provide any compliance artifacts you can share (SOC2, penetration test summary).

Regards,
Orion Health Security — on behalf of the compliance committee

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Orion Health Security <security@orionhealth.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing note — initial capacity targets

Hi all —

Quick consolidated answers and commercial next steps: point answers below; Karthik/Vivek to follow with artifacts.

1) Dedicated KMS: We support BYOK via customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS) and can integrate HSM-backed keys in the key policy. For Dedicated pools we map customer keys to the dedicated tenant and persist encrypted artifacts to the customer-designated S3 bucket.

2) Audit logs: We provide structured JSON logs (request_id, model, prompt_hash, timestamp, latency_ms, tenant_id, audit_tag). Retention is configurable; we can forward to your S3 with lifecycle rules you control for immutable retention. We'll share a sample log schema in the next email.

3) Private patching: For Private deployments, Redwood offers two models: (a) Customer-managed infra — you own patching; (b) Redwood-managed private — we operate the runtime in your VPC with maintenance windows agreed in the MSA. Security bulletins: published to your customer portal + emailed to security contacts. Incident response: we provide a named responder and 4-hour initial response SLA for enterprise contracts.

Commercial: We can quote both options. For this deal size (DEAL-2026-0421) we can offer a 6-month ramp credit on Dedicated reserved capacity (to offset initial scale-up) and a discounted onboarding fee for Private if you sign a 12‑month support contract.

Please confirm which path procurement prefers (Dedicated commit + support vs Private onboarding) and we will issue formal SOW/quote and send SOC2 + pen-test summary via secure link.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: orion_regulatory_requirements_2026.pdf
